mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above the prior quarter's median triggers a risk-off sentiment that compresses equity discount rates, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above its prior quarter median by at least 25 bps
regime_hint: early stage of a tightening cycle
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns in this regime are not statistically different from a pre-tightening baseline (p > 0.1), or FEDFUNDS does not exceed the median threshold in 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: Persistent declines in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) below the prior 12-month average indicate disinflation, which reduces policy rate expectations and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL falls for 4 consecutive months below its 12-month rolling average
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over this window are negative in >70% of similar 60-day periods since 2000, or CPIAUCSL fails to break the downward trend for >6 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden rise in employment growth (PAYEMS) above the prior quarter's mean coincides with stronger consumer confidence and supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS exceeds prior quarter mean by at least 10,000 jobs in a single month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are negative in >50% of analogous labor-expansion episodes since 1990, or employment growth decelerates sharply within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) signals weakening domestic demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls by at least 2.0% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during similar INDPRO contractions are not significantly negative (p > 0.15), or INDPRO recovers within 3 months.

mechanism_narrative: A multi-month decline in residential construction (assumed proxy via HOUST) indicates softening housing demand, which lowers growth expectations and yields negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls for 3 consecutive months below its 12-month moving average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from prior periods with similar HOUST declines (p > 0.1), or HOUST recovers within 2 months.

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both employment (PAYEMS) and consumer spending (RSAFS) above trend lines for two months creates a dual-demand bulge that supports positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS > 12-month mean AND RSAFS > 12-month mean for two consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX 20-day forward returns over this window are negative in >80% of analogous dual-demand episodes since 1995, or either PAYEMS or RSAFS reverts to trend within 4 months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment (UNRATE) above 5.0% signals policy tightening, which increases real discount rates and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days in a recessionary regime.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 5.0% in a month when GDP growth is negative
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during similar UNRATE spikes are not negative (p > 0.2), or GDP growth is positive during the same period.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for 4 consecutive months indicates supply-side softness that persists into the next quarter, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO falls for 4 consecutive months below its 3-month moving average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns during analogous INDPRO weakness are not significantly negative (p > 0.15), or INDPRO recovers by the end of the next quarter.
